== History ==
In the 3rd year of {{ill|Tengyō|en|Tengyō|qid=Q1327340|lt=Tenkyo}} (940), {{ill|Taira no Yoshifumi|en|Taira no Yoshifumi|qid=Q11483528|lt=Muraoka Gorō Yoshifumi}} enshrined for the purpose of praying for the defeat of {{ill|Taira no Masakado|ja|Taira no Masakado|2=en|3=Taira no Masakado|4=ja|5=平将門|6=de|7=Taira no Masakado|8=es|9=Taira no Masakado|10=fr|11=Taira no Masakado|lt=Taira no Masakado|qid=Q1207652|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira Masakado|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira no Masakado|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} by invoking the enshrinement from the {{ill|Kamigoryō Shrine|ja|上御霊神社|lt=Goryō Shrine|lt_ja=御霊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigorei Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11359018}} of Rakuchu == Subshrines ==
* {{ill|The Twelve Heavenly Kings|ja|十二天王|qid=Q140446401}}
* {{ill|Smallpox demon|en|Smallpox demon|qid=Q7543689|lt=Smallpox Deity}}
* Yatake {{ill|Inari Ōkami|abstract|Q719665|ar|إناري|az|İnari Okami|ban|Inari (Kami)|bcl|Inari Ōkami|ca|Oinari|cs|Inari (mytologie)|da|Inari|de|Inari (Kami)|el|Ινάρι Όκαμι|es|Inari (Japón)|et|Inari (jumal)|eu|Inari Ōkami|fa|ایناری|fi|Inari (kami)|fr|Inari (divinité japonaise)|hr|Inari|hu|Inari (sintó)|hy|Ինարի Օկամի|id|Inari (Kami)|it|Inari (mitologia)|ja|稲荷神|jv|Inari (Kami)|ko|이나리노카미|mni|ꯏꯅꯔꯤ ꯑꯣꯀꯃꯤ|ne|इनारी ओकामी|nl|Inari Ōkami|no|Inari|pl|Inari (bóstwo)|pt|Inari Ōkami|ru|Инари (божество)|simple|Inari Ōkami|sl|Inari (mitologija)|sr|Инари (богиња)|sv|Inari|tok|jan sewi suli Inali|tr|Inari Ōkami|uk|Інарі (міфологія)|vi|Inari Ōkami|zh|稻荷神|qid=Q719665|lt=Great Inari}} – also written as Ori-sasa Yatake Inari or Sasa-ori Yatake Inari. It is said that {{ill|Kamakura Gongorō Kagemasa|fr|Kamakura Gongorō Kagemasa|it|Kamakura Gongorō Kagemasa|ja|鎌倉景正|pt|Kamakura Gongorō Kagemasa|qid=Q1154948}}, during the {{ill|Gosannen War|en|Gosannen War|qid=Q1187411|lt=Later Three Years' War}}, had an arrow rebound after one of his eyes was struck, defeating his enemy. When that arrow was driven into the ground, bamboo sprang up, and thus Yatake Inari was enshrined.<ref>{{ill|Fujisawa Place Names 3rd Edition|ja|藤沢の地名 第3版|lt=Fujisawa Place Names, 3rd Edition, 1997}} 99, 100 pages.</ref>
* {{ill|Seven-Faced Shrine|ja|七面宮}}
== Branch Shrines ==
Owing to its proximity to the ruins of Muraoka Castle—the former residence of {{ill|Taira no Yoshifumi|en|Taira no Yoshifumi|qid=Q11483528|lt=Muraoka Gorō Yoshifumi}}—located in Muraoka Castle Ruins Park (28-2 Muraoka Higashi 3-chōme, {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|qid=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa City}}) (<nowiki>{{Coord|35|20|40.4|N|139|30|27.8|E|region:JP|name=村岡城址}}</nowiki>), there are 16 shrines in the prefecture said to have branched off from this shrine via {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|qid=Q195793|lt=Branching of Spirit}}. These include, for example, the shrine in Kamakura City – {{ill|Goryō Shrine (Kamakura City)|ja|御霊神社 (鎌倉市)|lt=Goryo Shrine|lt_ja=御霊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goryō Shrine (Kamakura)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11489364}}, the one in Hayama Town – {{ill|Goryō Shrine (Hayama Town)|ja|御霊神社 (葉山町)|lt=Goryo Shrine|lt_ja=御霊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goryō Shrine (Hayama)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11489362}}, and Kumano Shrine in Ōoba, {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|qid=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa City}}, also identified with the former {{ill|Ooba Shrine|ja|大庭神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ooba Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11435394}}, as well as other shrines of the same lineage such as {{ill|Kumano shrine|ja|大庭神社#熊野神社（藤沢市大庭）|lt=Kumano Shrine}}.

== Other ==
* Hatadateyama – The hill extending east of Goryō Shrine, also known as Heitan, is so named because {{ill|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|en|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|qid=Q3082851|lt=Minamoto no Yoriyoshi}} raised a white flag here to rally his troops.<ref>{{ill|Fujisawa Place Names 3rd Edition|ja|藤沢の地名 第3版|lt=Fujisawa Place Names, 3rd Edition, 1997}} 100 pages.</ref>

== History ==
In the 3rd year of {{ill|Tengyō|en|Tengyō|qid=Q1327340|lt=Tenkyo}} (940), {{ill|Taira no Yoshifumi|en|Taira no Yoshifumi|qid=Q11483528|lt=Muraoka Gorō Yoshifumi}} enshrined for the purpose of praying for the defeat of {{ill|Taira no Masakado|ja|Taira no Masakado|2=en|3=Taira no Masakado|4=ja|5=平将門|6=de|7=Taira no Masakado|8=es|9=Taira no Masakado|10=fr|11=Taira no Masakado|lt=Taira no Masakado|qid=Q1207652|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira Masakado|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira no Masakado|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} by invoking the enshrinement from the {{ill|Kamigoryō Shrine|ja|上御霊神社|lt=Goryō Shrine|lt_ja=御霊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigorei Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11359018}} of Rakuchu * {{ill|Smallpox demon|en|Smallpox demon|qid=Q7543689|lt=Smallpox Deity}}
* Yatake {{ill|Inari Ōkami|abstract|Q719665|ar|إناري|az|İnari Okami|ban|Inari (Kami)|bcl|Inari Ōkami|ca|Oinari|cs|Inari (mytologie)|da|Inari|de|Inari (Kami)|el|Ινάρι Όκαμι|es|Inari (Japón)|et|Inari (jumal)|eu|Inari Ōkami|fa|ایناری|fi|Inari (kami)|fr|Inari (divinité japonaise)|hr|Inari|hu|Inari (sintó)|hy|Ինարի Օկամի|id|Inari (Kami)|it|Inari (mitologia)|ja|稲荷神|jv|Inari (Kami)|ko|이나리노카미|mni|ꯏꯅꯔꯤ ꯑꯣꯀꯃꯤ|ne|इनारी ओकामी|nl|Inari Ōkami|no|Inari|pl|Inari (bóstwo)|pt|Inari Ōkami|ru|Инари (божество)|simple|Inari Ōkami|sl|Inari (mitologija)|sr|Инари (богиња)|sv|Inari|tok|jan sewi suli Inali|tr|Inari Ōkami|uk|Інарі (міфологія)|vi|Inari Ōkami|zh|稻荷神|qid=Q719665|lt=Great Inari}} – also written as Ori-sasa Yatake Inari or Sasa-ori Yatake Inari. It is said that {{ill|Kamakura Gongorō Kagemasa|fr|Kamakura Gongorō Kagemasa|it|Kamakura Gongorō Kagemasa|ja|鎌倉景正|pt|Kamakura Gongorō Kagemasa|qid=Q1154948}}, during the {{ill|Gosannen War|en|Gosannen War|qid=Q1187411|lt=Later Three Years' War}}, had an arrow rebound after one of his eyes was struck, defeating his enemy. When that arrow was driven into the ground, bamboo sprang up, and thus Yatake Inari was enshrined.<ref>{{ill|Fujisawa Place Names 3rd Edition|ja|藤沢の地名 第3版|lt=Fujisawa Place Names, 3rd Edition, 1997}} 99, 100 pages.</ref>
* {{ill|Seven-Faced Shrine|ja|七面宮}}

== Branch Shrines ==
Owing to its proximity to the ruins of Muraoka Castle—the former residence of {{ill|Taira no Yoshifumi|en|Taira no Yoshifumi|qid=Q11483528|lt=Muraoka Gorō Yoshifumi}}—located in Muraoka Castle Ruins Park (28-2 Muraoka Higashi 3-chōme, {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|qid=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa City}}) (<nowiki>{{Coord|35|20|40.4|N|139|30|27.8|E|region:JP|name=村岡城址}}</nowiki>), there are 16 shrines in the prefecture said to have branched off from this shrine via {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|qid=Q195793|lt=Branching of Spirit}}. These include, for example, the shrine in Kamakura City – {{ill|Goryō Shrine (Kamakura City)|ja|御霊神社 (鎌倉市)|lt=Goryo Shrine|lt_ja=御霊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goryō Shrine (Kamakura)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11489364}}, the one in Hayama Town – {{ill|Goryō Shrine (Hayama Town)|ja|御霊神社 (葉山町)|lt=Goryo Shrine|lt_ja=御霊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goryō Shrine (Hayama)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11489362}}, and Kumano Shrine in Ōoba, {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|qid=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa City}}, also identified with the former {{ill|Ooba Shrine|ja|大庭神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ooba Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11435394}}, as well as other shrines of the same lineage such as {{ill|Kumano shrine|ja|大庭神社#熊野神社（藤沢市大庭）|lt=Kumano Shrine}}.

* Hatadateyama – The hill extending east of Goryō Shrine, also known as Heitan, is so named because {{ill|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|en|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|qid=Q3082851|lt=Minamoto no Yoriyoshi}} raised a white flag here to rally his troops.<ref>{{ill|Fujisawa Place Names 3rd Edition|ja|藤沢の地名 第3版|lt=Fujisawa Place Names, 3rd Edition, 1997}} 100 pages.</ref>
